column1: # Tracked programs that `bin/kofun build` neither builds nor refuses by name
# THE PROPERTY THIS LEDGER IS THE EXCEPTION LIST FOR, stated once so a future
# gate can cite it rather than restate it:
#     IF `bin/kofun build` DOES NOT REFUSE A PROGRAM WITH AN `error[...]`
#     DIAGNOSTIC, THEN THE C IT WROTE MUST COMPILE.
# It is much weaker than "the compiler is correct" and entirely mechanical. A
# violation is a program the compiler said yes to and then handed to `cc`, which
# said no — and the author is shown a message about generated code at a byte
# offset in a file they did not write.
# `tests/emission/check.sh` sorts every tracked `*.kofun` into three outcomes:
# built, refused by name, or neither. The third is what this file lists, and it
# fails in BOTH directions the way `tests/backlog/debt.tsv` and
# `tests/pair-coverage/driver-failures.tsv` do: an unlisted violation is new
# drift, and a listed row that now builds or is refused is an improvement that
# was not recorded.
# MEASURED 2026-08-29 on origin/main@3d0e2a2f69667acb5914a82d46ef357b14703c07,
# over all 1320 tracked *.kofun: 358 built, 940 refused by name, 22 here.
# 249 seconds serially on an 8-core x86-64 Linux box, which is why the owning
# task is not in `task verify` and carries a row in
# tooling/gate-reachability/unreachable.tsv saying so.
# THE THREE KINDS, and why they are separate. An exemption folded into a drift
# ledger is indistinguishable from drift, and would be "fixed" by someone
# inventing the missing value — the same reasoning `stateless-tracker` and
# `capability-blocker` carry in tests/backlog/debt.tsv.
#   other-driver       The fixture belongs to a driver other than the default
#                      C path — the native, wasm, or selfhost-A1 corpora. Its
#                      owning gate compiles it with its own translation units
#                      and flags. Running the default driver over it is the
#                      WRONG INVOCATION, not a defect, and the row retires when
#                      the file stops being tracked or its driver changes.
#   seed-include-path  bootstrap/stage1/compiler.kofun, which emits C that
#                      includes `kofun_unicode.c`. Its own build supplies that
#                      translation unit; the default driver does not.
#   emission-defect    A REAL VIOLATION of the property above, on a file the
#                      default driver owns. #1539 predicted this set would be
#                      empty — "it finds nothing new, because those files
#                      already build in some gate". It is not empty. Owner:
# path

column1: bootstrap/native/fixtures/function_int64_too_large.kofun
column3: Native backend fixture. `task native` builds it through the native image writer, which is where its INT64 bound is decided; the C path emits INT64_C(9223372036854775808) and gcc calls that unsigned.

column3: Native backend fixture measuring frame layout at the local-count boundary. The C path emits a binding the fixture never reads, which is -Werror=unused-variable there and the whole point of the fixture in the native lowering.

column1: tests/conformance/inference/hm-levels/recursion.kofun
column3: #1628. `recursion.c:235: error: 'k_b1' undeclared (first use in this function)`, and `kofun_lambda_1` is emitted and never called. The emitter wrote a reference to a variable it never declared — the same class as #1622's `lambda_scope`, on the emission side. The sharpest of the three and not a flag artifact.
